Division by the degree agrees with pinned Heights/Absolute/Basic.lean logHeight_one_eq_gen. Computing instead in the full point field gives the same value by logHeight_comp_ringHom. A regular zero evaluates to [1:0], also of height zero; no pole order is being mistaken for a value or included in an arithmetic height sum.

These formulas match pinned Belyi/CurveField/Canonical.lean:72-79. In particular a simple pole contributes -2, not 0 or +2. The exact coefficient constraint uniquely determines D.

For the smooth Fermat curve the coordinate poles at infinity are simultaneous simple poles; the divisor has total degree N over Q, counting residue degrees and all infinity points.

findings.conclusion: The adjunction equation has the right divisor and sign, with a concrete possible rational function.
findings.reason: For N>0 in characteristic zero, the differential du/v^(N-1) has divisor (N-3)H. Hence div(du)=(N-3)H+div(v^(N-1)), so r=v^(N-1) supplies the indicated sign. v is nonzero since otherwise the Fermat equation would make the transcendental u algebraic. The structure does not postulate any height estimate.

Each finite place is counted once exactly when some value has norm greater than one; its contribution is log of its residue-field absolute norm, divided by [x.fieldOf:Q]. Finite G implies finite support, including when some generator evaluates to zero. The out-of-domain zero branch is the source totalization and is not used by the comparisons.

Degree-bounded points have bounded local degrees, which is essential because PadicAlgCl itself is not locally compact. findings.reason: Every embedding of Q(phi(x)) into either algebraically closed local target extends to x.fieldOf, so the full-point LocalBounds descend to all image embeddings. At a finite place over 2, pinned Heights/Local/PlaceEmbedding.lean:332 gives w(y)=norm(tau(y))^m with 0<m<=[Q(phi(x)):Q]<=x.degree<=d. Thus absolute log w(y)<=d*max(c,0). findings.conclusion: CanonicalDegreeIdentity is correct for N>3 and actual adjunction inputs.

findings.conclusion: CanonicalHeightIdentification has the correct fixed height and normalization.
findings.reason: The divisor divdu is linearly equivalent to (N-3)H. The height of H is the absolute projective height of [u:v:1]. At affine points the existing Fermat.projectiveHeight computes exactly this height in Q(u(x),v(x)), normalized by its degree. Thus every chosen canonical polar height differs from the existing Fermat.canonicalHeight=(N-3)*projectiveHeight by a bounded amount uniformly over all algebraic points. findings.reason: For a Belyi phi, div(dphi)+E is linearly equivalent to the polar divisor of phi. divdu and divdphi are linearly equivalent, since their ratio is a nonzero rational function. It holds uniformly over all Qbar points, including poles, and allows negative q where the degree inequality permits it. Constants may depend on both presentations. In the image field the three values phi, inverse phi and inverse(1-phi) detect exactly the tripod bad primes, including zeros, ones and poles modulo primes. Their images occur among G values. findings.conclusion: The five height/arithmetic comparisons plus canonical degree, local images and concrete choices suffice for the original CanonicalEstimate.

findings.conclusion: The final contradiction has the correct coefficients and does not switch the parent height.
findings.reason: Write H for fixed Fermat.canonicalHeight, D for fixed Fermat.logDiff, hK and hE for the two actual polar heights. The chosen q=max(degE/degK,0)+1 is positive and strictly exceeds the ratio. delta=epsilon/(1+q*(1+epsilon)) gives a=1-delta*q>0 and 1+delta=(1+epsilon)*a. Hence a*H<=(1+epsilon)*a*D+C. Failure points satisfy H>(1+epsilon)*D+s(n); strict monotonicity gives s(n)>=n, so selecting n>C/a contradicts the preceding bound. No nonnegativity of D is needed and no illicit dropping of a signed term occurs.
